notes: Hermes is a pre-session adapter: wiring.go turns its CommandPattern into the scanner's pgrep -f match, so a proc-<PID> row is born in ready for the live `hermes chat` process, and the store's own session id (<YYYYMMDD>_<HHMMSS>_<hex>) reconciles under a DIFFERENT id only once the sessions row is INSERTed — which hermes does on the FIRST USER MESSAGE, not at launch. Each variant is therefore modelled as two births (vN_session_birth = proc row, vN_handoff = store session) and every later phase anchors to the handoff. Phase order follows the recipe's variant chain: (1) clean Ctrl-D exit, (2) SIGKILL mid-idle, (3) SIGKILL mid-turn. Spec assertions: v1 'State is ready at exit' (hermes writes ended_at/end_reason='cli_close' on the way out, so the final ready is store-derived AND precedes process_exited); v2 'state never re-enters working/waiting once idle'; v3 'state does not stick in working' — for v2/v3 the store never gets an ended_at at all (a killed process runs no finally), so the daemon's process-exit sweep is the only settle path. Prompts are sized to outlive the watcher's 2s poll: a turn that finishes inside one poll would be first observed already carrying finish_reason='stop' and the working leg would never appear. observations pin no model (the recording home's config.yaml decides it) and assert tokens only — hermes reports estimated_cost_usd 0.0 under billing_mode='subscription_included' and its model slug is not in aliases.go, so cost is expected to be 0.

text: Variant 1: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready once the hermes REPL process is up (the TUI boot is slow — 35 tools + 68 skills — so the budget is generous)
Variant 1: the store's session row is INSERTed on the first user message and reconciles under a different session_id; it never enters waiting over its lifetime
Variant 1: the in-flight turn drives the store session ready → working (newest message is not yet assistant/finish_reason='stop')
Variant 1: assistant row lands with finish_reason='stop' — the explicit turn boundary — and the session returns to ready

Variant 1: clean Ctrl-D exit — hermes writes ended_at + end_reason='cli_close' and then the process goes, so process_exited fires AFTER state returned to ready (the v1_turn_done → v1_exit chain proves 'State is ready at exit')
Variant 2: a new proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready after variant 1 finishes and the REPL is relaunched in a fresh cwd
Variant 2: the second store session reconciles under a different session_id; never enters waiting over its lifetime
Variant 2: the in-flight turn drives the store session ready → working
Variant 2: turn completes back to ready; over the ensuing idle window (through the kill) the session never re-enters working or waiting (satisfies 'State never entered working post-exit')

Variant 2: SIGKILL mid-idle — the store row keeps ended_at NULL (a killed process runs no finally), so process_exited from the daemon's PID sweep is the only settle signal, and it fires while the session is in ready
Variant 3: a new proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready after variant 2 finishes
Variant 3: the third store session reconciles under a different session_id; never enters waiting over its lifetime
Variant 3: the long generation drives the store session ready → working; the recipe waits 8s before killing so this leg is observed rather than skipped

Variant 3: SIGKILL mid-turn — process_exited fires while the session is still in working, proving the state does not stick there (the live sweep-to-ready may not appear inside the recording's 8s tail, per the recipe's notes)
